test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7th December 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Raining cats and dogs
solution:
The correct answer is Raining heavily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'raining cats and dogs' is 'raining heavily'.
 
• Raining Cats and Dogs: To rain very heavily.
 
 
• Example: Don't forget to take your umbrella - it's raining cats and dogs out there.
 
 
 
• Therefore from the above-mentioned points, we can conclude that option 4 is the correct answer.

 

Correct sentence: Raining heavily.
